title: Mites
subtitle: Based on Mitch's answers and the product labels, checked against NSW requirements. Updated 6 Nov 2026.
source: Mitch's answers 6 Nov 2026; LPC Tech Onboarding Pack (PPE, never list, if something goes wrong); jobbook-data/services.json and past job wordings (mite and tick jobs); jobbook-data/chemicals.json (product names); researched, not from Mitch: SA Health bird mites fact sheet (2025)

sections.heading: When this job comes up
body: Customer has mites, for example bird, clover or rodent mites. There are many different kinds. Mitch can't really tell them apart and the treatment is similar for all of them, so you don't need to name the mite to do the job.
The job process, the never list, PPE and the free service period are in the Every job guide.

sections.heading: What the law and the label require

items.text: Follow the product label
items.detail: Using a pesticide against its label is an offence. If the job needs something the label does not allow, stop and call Mitch.

items.text: Make the record the same day
items.detail: Every pesticide job needs a record: full product name, date, target pest, rate and quantity, address and area treated, who applied it, equipment, and start and finish times. It must be made within 48 hours and kept at least 3 years. Give the customer a copy if they ask.

items.text: Outdoor spraying: record the weather
items.detail: Write down wind speed and direction at the start and whenever it changes. Add temperature, humidity or rain if the label says it matters. A subfloor outside the walls counts as outdoors.

items.text: Keep it out of waterways
items.detail: Never spray near waterways, ponds, tanks or fish. Check the label for the distance.

items.text: Only do work your licence covers
items.detail: If a treatment is outside your licence class, work under Mitch's direct supervision and do not do it alone.

items.text: Protect people, pets and the environment
items.detail: Wear the PPE the label and SDS call for. Keep spray and bait away from people, pets, food, drains and waterways. Harming people, wildlife or property with a pesticide is an offence.

items.text: Roof voids and subfloors: asbestos
items.detail: Houses built before 1990 can have asbestos (roof insulation, eaves, cladding). Do not disturb anything that might be asbestos. Stop and tell Mitch.

items.text: Roof voids: live wiring
items.detail: Look first. Do not touch cables. If you are not sure it is safe, do not go in and tell Mitch.

items.text: Tight or stuffy spaces
items.detail: If you cannot get out easily, or the air feels wrong, do not go in. Tell Mitch first.

sections.heading: PPE
sections.title: PPE on before you go in
sections.note: Never apply chemicals without PPE. If the SDS requires it, you wear it. No exceptions.
items: Gloves and closed shoes at minimum
Gloves, mask and eye protection for any spray, as per the product SDS

items.text: Roof void entry: dust mask, gloves, torch, appropriate footwear

sections.heading: Products Mitch uses
sections.title: Names as in Mitch's product list. No rates here: follow the label. Mitch uses bifenthrin and Coopex, and Astro usually in cars. Use whichever bifenthrin Mitch has loaded, after checking its label covers this pest and the place you are treating.
rows: Bifenthrin (Country Bifenthrin 100 Low Odour or Aquastar 100SC)
Astro Aerosol Residual Insecticide (usually in cars)

sections.heading: Steps
sections.title: Steps
items: Ask the customer to point out where the problem is and where the bites happen
Take BEFORE photos of the problem areas

items.text: Take a torch and have a good look
items.detail: Start with what the customer shows you. For bird mites, look for the bird nest: eaves, roof space, wall cavities, chimneys, porches and window ledges.

items.text: Treat the source if you can
items.detail: Nests, roosts or whatever is feeding the mites. Wear a mask and gloves if you remove a bird nest. If it is hard to reach, leave it for a builder or the customer.

items.text: Treat the areas around it too
items.detail: Ceiling voids, walls and cavities, skirting and soft furnishings. Use bifenthrin and Coopex. Use your judgement on how far to go: inside, the outside perimeter, gardens and soil, a mattress or a car, or a partial treatment.

items.text: Cars: Astro is what Mitch usually uses
items.detail: Cars: Astro is Mitch's usual. Mattresses: only with a product whose label allows it. Mitch will show you on the ride-along.

items.text: Apply per the product label. Never exceed label rates
items.detail: Never mix chemicals without checking the label first. If in doubt, call Mitch.

items: Keep chemicals away from food, children and pets
Note anything you could not treat or reach, and why

items.text: Tell the customer a hot wash is advised
items.detail: Linen and soft items.

items.text: Always advise a second treatment
items.detail: It breaks the mite cycle. Most jobs need one.

sections.heading: Job complete when
items: The source treated if it could be, and the areas around it
Anything you could not treat or reach is noted on the job report, with the reason
Product, rate, area and quantity recorded on the job report
Customer told what you did, to hot wash linen and soft items, and that a second treatment is advised to break the cycle
Customer told they can go back in once it has dried, as the product label says
Service report left, or customer told it is being emailed

items.q: How long before I can go back in?
items.a: Pretty soon, once it has dried. Follow the product label.

items.q: Why do I need a second treatment?
items.a: It breaks the mite cycle. One treatment often isn't enough.
Bird mites don't live on people. They can only complete their life cycle on a bird, so they bite and move on.

items.q: How long until they are gone?
items.a: Bird mites generally die within 3 weeks without a bird to feed on, and they tend to clear up once the birds and nests are gone. We treat the area as well.
Itchy, swollen, raised red spots. They are often mistaken for other bites. They are not linked to spreading disease.

sections.heading: Tell Mitch straight away if
sections.body: Call Mitch on 0432 181 689. After hours or urgent, call Mitch directly.

items.text: You apply the wrong chemical
items.detail: Stop immediately. Do not continue. Call Mitch.

items.text: There is a spill
items.detail: Follow the SDS procedure. Call Mitch immediately. Never leave a spill unattended.

items.text: Someone is hurt
items.detail: Treat the injury first. Call Mitch. Write down what happened.

items.text: The customer complains or gets aggressive
items.detail: Stay calm and do not argue. For a complaint, tell them Mitch will call them today. If they are aggressive, remove yourself. Call Mitch either way.

items.text: The customer asks for a quote on anything complex, or you are not sure
items.detail: Say "I'll need to get Mitch to come and have a look and provide a quote for that."

items.text: You see signs of termites or other pests outside this job
items.detail: Photograph it and tell Mitch. Termite quotes always go to Mitch.

Law and safety points checked on 6 Nov 2026 against the NSW Pesticides Regulation 2017 (clauses 35 to 37 on records and 13 to 16 on supervision, as published by the NSW EPA) and SafeWork NSW pages. Changes to the Regulation since 2017 were not checked.
